text: Setting clear goals is essential for any project's success. A useful framework is to create SMART goals, which are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. Instead of a vague aim like "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase monthly sign-ups by 15% within three months." Once your main goal is set, break it down into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress, and each milestone should have clear deliverables—tangible results, such as a design mockup or a final report. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment by communicating these goals and milestones with everyone involved. When all parties agree on the direction and definition of success, the team can work together effectively and avoid confusion.
